title: vendor table restructured overnight: scraper returned 200 OK with fewer keys per row
recipe: anchor re-derived selectors on the last-good field VALUES rather than on markup, then refuse the repair unless health passes on the new spec

problem.symptom: A scraper returns HTTP 200 and the expected number of rows, but fields are silently missing from every row.
problem.context: A collector pointed at a vendor page that was restructured overnight.
problem.detected_by: scrape.schema — required-field and type conformance, not HTTP status

diagnosis.root_cause: Selectors were anchored to markup. The markup changed; the data did not.
diagnosis.why_it_happens: This is the failure mode that matters and the one nobody catches: the request succeeds, so error handling never fires. A missing price is not an exception, it is a None that flows downstream.
diagnosis.confirm_with: Compare row count and per-field fill rate against the last good baseline. A 200 with fewer keys per row is the signature.

fix.summary: Re-derive selectors by anchoring on the last-good field *values* rather than on tags or classes, then refuse the repair unless health passes on the new spec.

steps.why: exit 1 means drift, not a network error
proposes a new spec; writes nothing
a human sees the change before it lands
only after the diff is reviewed

fix.code:
# anchor on data, not markup: find the element whose text equals a
# known-good value, then derive its selector from that position

verification.expected: check exits 0 with the original row count restored and every required field present.

applies_when: a scraper's output shape changed without an error
a last-good extraction exists to anchor on
does_not_apply_when: there is no last-good baseline — there is nothing to anchor to and the repair has no ground truth
the site genuinely stopped publishing the field; re-deriving a selector for data that no longer exists will produce a confident empty column
the page is behind a login or renders client-side only
preconditions: a baseline with per-field fill rates
